title: Google Plans 2.7 GW Power Capacity for New $17B Wyoming AI Campus

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Google is establishing its first Wyoming data center hub with a plan to build a computing campus on 716 acres in Laramie County. Known as Project Tembo, the $17 billion venture will consist of four data center halls near Cheyenne and is scheduled to begin operation in the second half of 2028. The facility is expected to start with a power capacity of 2.7 GW, though company plans include eventually scaling the site's capacity to 10 GW by the time construction is completed in 2031.

The project is expected to create roughly 3,700 annual jobs, though Google will hire only 250 employees directly. Statewide construction for the hub will support more than 8,800 jobs, with about 2,500 workers on site during peak building phases. To bring the project to fruition, Google acquired the land and regulatory approvals from developer Crusoe, assuming direct control of the site's management.

To power the campus, American Electric Power will invest $4B in a 702 MW natural gas fuel cell plant utilizing Bloom Energy cells under a 20 year agreement. To mitigate environmental impact, Google will use air-cooling systems to save water and route captured carbon to a sequestration hub operated by Tallgrass Energy. The company stated it will pay for all electricity consumed and infrastructure costs driven by the growth of the site.

selectedTweets.text:
GOOGLE $GOOGL BUYS CRUSOE'S WYOMING DATA CENTER SITE

• The sale completes Crusoe's pre-development work on the southeast Wyoming campus, including site selection, government approvals and power strategy
• Crusoe and Tallgrass Energy started the project, planning power from fuel cells, the grid and natural gas turbines
• Crusoe is also the developer of Google's data center campus under construction outside Amarillo, Texas

Terms weren't disclosed. Crusoe says it has more than 6 GW contracted and over 40 GW in its pipeline, per a Crusoe release.

selectedTweets.bestBit: Google says construction will support more than 8,800 jobs statewide, with about 2,500 workers on site at peak.
selectedTweets.text:
GOOGLE IS PUTTING $17 BILLION INTO WYOMING. IT COMES WITH 250 GOOGLE JOBS.

Google just confirmed its first Wyoming data center, a campus in Laramie County near Cheyenne.

The build is the big part. Google says construction will support more than 8,800 jobs statewide, with about 2,500 workers on site at peak. Those are construction jobs. They wind down as the buildings finish.

Once it runs, Google says the site will support over 3,700 jobs a year. Only 250 of those are roles Google creates directly. That is about $68 million of investment for each one.

The power side alone is huge. AEP is building a 702 MW fuel cell plant for the campus, running on natural gas with Bloom Energy cells.

This is what tech growth looks like now. Billions go into buildings and electricity. A few hundred people run them. 

I just wonder if they will be American jobs...
